evidence: app/src/lib/queries.ts (entire file) — all API access lives behind one module with view-model interfaces (PokemonPageData, MoveTableData…), so a backend change is contained here; good boundary design

app/src/lib/queries.ts:118-120, 214-216, 236-241, 271-276, 481-489 — five separate hand-rolled memoized promise caches (`jsonCache`, `speciesDirectoryPromise`, `generationPromise`, `typeDataPromise`, `homePromise`, `versionGroupsPromise`) with no TTL or invalidation; data changes require a process restart

app/src/lib/queries.ts:401-403, 484-489, 494-498, 549-568 — PokeAPI responses consumed as `any` (`Map<string, any>`, `node: any`, `(entry: any)`), so schema drift is a runtime failure, not a compile error

app/src/routes/index.tsx:9-12 — `paramValue` re-implements the router's `string | string[]` param resolution by hand instead of the library helper
app/src/routes/index.tsx:131-133, 75-82 — `attr:value` plus a manual `searchInput.value = …` write in a `createEffect`; the framework `value` prop would stay consistent for free

churn_resistance.rationale: The architecture ages well — one data module, one config file, framework-boilerplate limited to the two regenerable entry files — but the boundary itself is untyped `any` and never type-checked, there are no unit tests, and six hand-rolled caches with no invalidation will all need rework the day data freshness or TTL matters.

findings.issue: No TypeScript tooling: `typescript` is not a dependency and no script runs `tsc --noEmit`, so the strict tsconfig (app/tsconfig.json:8) and all interface types are never actually checked by `vite build` or `npm test`.
findings.suggestion: Add `typescript` as a devDependency and a `"typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"` script run in CI (or chained into `build`).

findings.issue: PokeAPI responses are parsed as `any` throughout (`(entry: any)`, `Map<string, any>` at lines 484-489, `node: any` at 494-498, 549-568); schema drift becomes silent runtime breakage in an untyped, untested module.
findings.suggestion: Declare interfaces for the API records (PokemonRecord, MoveRecord, TypeRecord…) next to the view-model types, and validate at the fetch boundary.

findings.issue: Module-level promise caches (`jsonCache`, `speciesDirectoryPromise`, `homePromise`, `typeDataPromise`, `versionGroupsPromise`) are memoized forever with no TTL, eviction, or revalidation — the spec asks the API to be treated as live data, so any change never appears until the server restarts. The same hand-rolled memo pattern is copy-pasted six times.
findings.suggestion: Extract one `memoize(key, fn, ttl)` helper (or use the router query cache / `revalidate`) so freshness policy lives in one place and can be changed without touching six call sites.

findings.issue: `HttpStatusCode code={404}` is rendered from data-dependent branches (`Show when={data() === null}`) without `deferStream: true` on the `createAsync` calls (app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].tsx:128), so with streaming the status is likely set after the first flush and clients receive 200 (the known v2 issue solid-start#2229).
findings.suggestion: Pass `{ deferStream: true }` to `createAsync` on routes whose 404 state is derived from fetched data.

findings.issue: `nitro` is pinned to an exact dated pre-stable build (`3.0.260610-beta`); nitro 3 is still shipping breaking changes between betas/RCs (3.0.261029-rc current), so upgrades require manual edits and the app can silently miss fixes.
findings.suggestion: Track the framework's recommended install (`npm i nitro`) with a range, and note the pinned-rationale in a comment.

findings.issue: `attr:value` plus manual DOM sync via `createEffect` (lines 75-82) re-implements controlled-input behavior that Solid's `value` prop already provides reactively.
findings.suggestion: Use plain `value={searchText()}` and let the signal drive the input; delete the manual `searchInput.value = …` write.

findings.issue: `spriteForId` hardcodes the sprite URL pattern, coupling the app to the API's media layout instead of using the `sprites.front_default` the record already carries (which it does use for artwork at lines 549-556).
findings.suggestion: Where a pokemon record is already fetched, prefer its sprite fields; keep the pattern only for list endpoints that lack them, in one named constant.

findings.issue: `paramValue` hand-rolls `string | string[]` resolution that the router library already provides.
findings.suggestion: Use the router's param-resolution helper instead of a local copy, so router typing changes surface via the library rather than a stale local shim.

findings.issue: README and .gitignore (app/.gitignore:1-5, entries like `.vinxi`, `app.config.timestamp_*.js`) are v1-template boilerplate that no longer matches the v2 vite.config-based setup.
findings.suggestion: Regenerate the docs/ignore files from the current SolidStart v2 template so future contributors aren't pointed at v1-era knobs.

findings.issue: Zero test cases in the app: pure, high-traffic helpers like `humanize`, `latestEnglishFlavor`, `collapseWhitespace` and the sort comparator (app/src/components/MoveTable.tsx:12-29) have no unit coverage, so future framework or data changes regress silently.
findings.suggestion: Add a minimal vitest suite for lib/format.ts and the sort/missing-value logic; these are pure functions and cost nothing to test.

summary: This is a genuinely current SolidStart v2 codebase — the vite.config/nitro-plugin setup, query/createAsync data layer, meta handling and entry points all match the October 2026 stable docs exactly, and dependencies are the minimum the framework itself requires. The data layer is well centralized behind one typed view-model module, but that boundary is parsed as `any`, is never type-checked (no `typescript` in devDependencies, no tsc script) and is guarded by six never-invalidating hand-rolled promise caches. It will age acceptably, but tightening the API boundary and unifying the caching policy are the first things a future maintainer will have to touch.
